research

Gaze-Based Robot Failure Detection

Overview

This line of work investigates the relationship between human gaze behaviour and robot failures. Using robot-assisted collaborative tasks (such as tangram puzzles), I explore how different failure types affect human perception and gaze dynamics, presenting gaze as a potential signal for robot error detection and recovery.

Trust Dynamics Across Multiple Robot Failures

Overview

This study explores the dynamics of trust in human-robot collaboration in the context of repeated robot failures. It focuses on how the consistency of failure types and the robot's awareness of its own errors affect user perceptions of trust and intelligence.

Where Did You Look?

The Problem

Pick-and-place robots rely on sensing, planning and movement, and when one of them fails the robot often carries on as if nothing happened. In our study the robot failed in three ways. It froze mid-transport while still holding a piece, it placed a piece in the wrong location, or it closed its gripper on nothing and continued without the piece. When people work side by side with a robot, a missed failure stalls the task, breaks the rhythm of the collaboration and costs trust.
